1987

Serpent's Egg

The Magic Dozen and Inneall's Ocean in the Floating World

Set in the "Global Village" of 2035, a "Floating World" governed by the shadowy and near-invisible Kangaroo, an elitist interspecies authority that orders assassinations for the common good and eliminates dangerous "Serpent's Egg" experiments, those that succeed "only too well", through hybrid killers called the Dolophonoi.

The novel centers on the Lynn-Randal Experiment, which raised together three "super-mega-persons": Lord Randal, an "enhanced" human boy with an off-the-scale IQ; Axel, a gargoyle-faced Axel's Ape whose father founded an underground ape society; and Inneall, an Ambulatory Mime-Human Computer who insists she is the little girl "Bloody Mary Muldoon the Pirate Queen." Inneall created a vast, ever-expanding Ocean.

They are later merged with children from three other experiments to form the Magic Dozen: Marino (a young male seal), Luas (a young male angel), Henryetta (a fiery human girl), Lutin (a prophetic pythoness), Dubu (a young female bear), Schimp (a young male chimpanzee), Gajah (an unborn "Wonder of the World Elephant"), Carcajou (a wolverine of "evil intelligence"), and Popugai (a young male parrot). Guided by the wealthy surrogate grandfather Satrap Saint Ledger, the Dozen gather at Heart's Desire Cove on the shore of their Ocean, aware that as they near their tenth birthdays, the Kangaroo may judge them a Serpent's Egg. The story builds toward "The Three Days of Summerset," a time charged with foreboding.

Themes

Identity and hybridity Control versus autonomy Evolution of intelligence and species succession Perception and reality The nature of experimentation Fate and prophecy Artifice versus nature Memory, history, and narratives Morality and ethics

A-B-C Diagnostic

A: Reality Floating World and Inneall's Ocean

Reality is a "Floating World": "The Floating World was a giant boat or ark"; any heavier-than-water boat can sink if it ships enough water. Inneall created a vast, ever-expanding Ocean, "extents of water that are standing where no water stood yesterday." "The Castle named Domdaniel which is at the bottom of the Ocean."

B: Being Magic Dozen

Being is hybrid and experimental: Lord Randal (enhanced human), Axel (Axel's Ape), Inneall (Ambulatory Computer who made the Ocean), Marino (seal), Luas (angel), Lutin (pythoness), Dubu (bear), Schimp (chimpanzee), Gajah (unborn elephant), Carcajou (evil wolverine). "All of the underwater creatures live in an active state of churning unconsciousness"; "All of them live in dreamworlds."

C: Change Three Days of Summerset

Change comes as threat: the Kangaroo eliminates "Serpent's Egg" experiments through the Dolophonoi. As the Dozen approach their tenth birthdays, they may be judged dangerous. "The Ocean Metastasis, a dream state of incomparable vividness", "the Oceanic Hyper-Active Dream State." The question: "When the Sea Shall Give Up Its Dead."

A + B: Reality and Being Experimental Lives in the Floating World

The Magic Dozen come from four experiments that bring different forms of life and intelligence together. Inneall’s ocean then provides a new environment for their activity. The Ocean Metastasis allows them to enter its depths in a vivid dream state, extending what these experimental beings can experience.

A + C: Reality and Change Inneall's Ever-Expanding Ocean

Inneall created an Ocean that keeps expanding, swallowing roads and valleys. Her experiment targets the world itself, making water stand where none stood before. Such powers expose the children to the Kangaroo’s judgment that an experiment may succeed "only too well."

B + C: Being and Change The Dozen at Heart's Desire Cove

The twelve hybrid children, gathering at the shore of their own Ocean as their tenth birthdays approach, are the catalyst for transformation or destruction. Their very existence is the Serpent's Egg that might hatch into a new world or be eliminated by the Dolophonoi. Three Days of Summerset will decide.

Core Conflict

In the "Floating World" of 2035, the Magic Dozen, children from four experiments, face judgment from the Kangaroo authority as a "Serpent's Egg" that succeeds "only too well," while gathering at Heart's Desire Cove on the shore of Inneall's ever-expanding Ocean for "The Three Days of Summerset."

Sources for Serpent's Egg

R. A. Lafferty, Serpent's Egg. Morrigan Publications, 1987.

Thematic Clusters

Cross-Novel Synthesis

Thematic currents flowing through the oceanic corpus

The Domdaniel Thread

Domdaniel locates hidden powers beneath the sea. In Camels it houses an archetypal company; in East of Laughter it is the meeting place of the Ocean’s governors; in Fair Hills it belongs to an underwater political order. The castle conceals different kinds of authority: archetypal, economic, and political.

Aurelia East of Laughter Serpent's Egg Easterwine Camels Fair Hills

The Polluted Pool

In Sweeny, Widdershins describes collective consciousness as an oil-slick surface above depths haunted by the wars. Camels makes the shared ocean a medium open to purchased influence, while Sandaliotis places a national unconscious in submarine caves. Their depths hold different forms of concealed pressure: historical catastrophe, manipulation, and collective fear.

Sweeny Camels Sandaliotis

The Narrative Sea

Narrative enters these worlds in distinct ways. Space Chantey gives a voyage epic form; East of Laughter and Iron Tongue make the writing of scenarios part of the world’s operation; Sweeny sets rival histories against one another. Klepsis makes access to history itself a problem. An ocean voyage can carry characters through an epic, into a mind, or toward the powers that write their world.

Klepsis Space Chantey East of Laughter Sweeny Iron Tongue

Crossings and Their Limits

Camels makes Prime World the feared end of world-jumping and evasion of judgment. Sandaliotis tests the apparent solidity of a country; Sindbad carries its quest among worlds and into hidden depths; Fair Hills opens a submerged civilization to land visitors. Pilgrim seeks passage out of judgment; the Fair Hills visitors enter the depths to discover who governs their world.

Camels Sandaliotis Sindbad Fair Hills

The Schizo-Gash

Divided being takes different forms: rival psychic powers in Fourth Mansions, programmed control in Past Master, alien belonging in The Reefs of Earth, and composite personhood in Easterwine. The recurring question is how a person can act with integrity under these different pressures.

Fourth Mansions Past Master Reefs of Earth Easterwine

The Hatching

Eggs, cocoons, and hidden depths give transformation the form of emergence. Serpent’s Egg places experimental lives under threat before maturity; The Elliptical Grave confines its investigators in a pavilion that is also grave, ark, and cocoon. Fourth Mansions makes mutation a contested passage, while Fair Hills brings the submerged world into contact with the surface.

Serpent's Egg Fourth Mansions Fair Hills Elliptical Grave
